root_cause.text: The QRTR-over-MHI receive path relied on MHI's DL `auto_queue` feature, which could invoke `dl_callback` and queue RX buffers before `qcom_mhi_qrtr_probe()` had fully initialized and registered the driver's `qrtr_mhi_dev` state, creating a probe-time race that led to NULL-pointer dereferences.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit message explicitly says "`dl_callback` for the DL channel may get called before the client driver is fully probed" and that internal code may call MHI queue APIs before `mhi_prepare_for_transfer_autoqueue()` is called, causing NULL dereferences; the patch removes all `.auto_queue = true` uses, replaces `mhi_prepare_for_transfer_autoqueue()` with `mhi_prepare_for_transfer()`, and makes QRTR manually queue/recycle DL buffers in `qcom_mhi_qrtr_queue_dl_buffers()` and `qcom_mhi_qrtr_dl_callback()`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit message explicitly says "`dl_callback` for the DL channel may get called before the client driver is fully probed" and that internal code may call MHI queue APIs before `mhi_prepare_for_transfer_autoqueue()` is called, causing NULL dereferences; the patch removes all `.auto_queue = true` uses, replaces `mhi_prepare_for_transfer_autoqueue()` with `mhi_prepare_for_transfer()`, and makes QRTR manually queue/recycle DL buffers in `qcom_mhi_qrtr_queue_dl_buffers()` and `qcom_mhi_qrtr_dl_callback()`.

intent_record.what: The `.auto_queue = false` field initializer was removed from one entry in the `ath12k_mhi_channels_wcn7850` static `mhi_channel_config` array.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this entry will no longer explicitly set `auto_queue` to false and will instead rely on the struct's default or zero-initialized value, which preserves the same effective behavior if false is the default.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop explicitly enabling auto_queue for the WCN7850 MHI channel so it falls back to the default queueing behavior.
intent_record.what: The `.auto_queue = true` field initializer was removed from a `struct mhi_channel_config` entry in the `ath12k_mhi_channels_wcn7850` channel configuration array.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this channel config will no longer explicitly enable `auto_queue`; the field will instead use the struct's implicit default value for an omitted initializer, which changes the queueing behavior for that MHI channel if the default is different from `true`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Handle MHI reset completions by freeing RX buffers and recycle successfully processed buffers back to the device to maintain correct receive-buffer management.
intent_record.what: The callback's early-return condition was changed to return only when qdev is NULL or when transaction_status is a nonzero error other than -ENOTCONN. A new special-case block was added to detect transaction_status == -ENOTCONN, free mhi_res->buf_addr with devm_kfree(), and return. After calling qrtr_endpoint_post(), new code was added to requeue the same receive buffer with mhi_queue_buf(..., DMA_FROM_DEVICE, mhi_res->buf_addr, mhi_dev->mhi_cntrl->buffer_len, MHI_EOT) and log an error if recycling fails.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the callback now treats channel reset/disconnect (-ENOTCONN) differently by freeing the receive buffer instead of silently returning. For successful or acceptable completions, it no longer leaves the consumed buffer unreused; instead it reposts the buffer back to MHI for future incoming data. This fixes receive-buffer lifecycle handling so buffers are either released on reset or recycled after packet delivery, preventing buffer loss and sustaining continued RX operation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add logic to allocate and queue all available downlink buffers so QRTR over MHI can receive incoming data reliably.
intent_record.what: A new static function, qcom_mhi_qrtr_queue_dl_buffers(struct mhi_device *mhi_dev), was added. It gets the number of free DMA_FROM_DEVICE descriptors via mhi_get_free_desc_count(), loops over each available descriptor, allocates a buffer of size mhi_dev->mhi_cntrl->buffer_len with devm_kmalloc(), queues each buffer with mhi_queue_buf(..., DMA_FROM_DEVICE, ..., MHI_EOT), and returns -ENOMEM on allocation failure or the queueing error after logging it with dev_err(). If all buffers are queued successfully, it returns 0.
intent_record.how: This change adds runtime logic to pre-fill all currently free downlink receive descriptors with allocated buffers, enabling incoming device-to-host data transfers to be received on all available DMA slots. It prevents the receive path from lacking queued buffers and surfaces allocation or queueing failures immediately.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix probe initialization ordering and cleanup by preparing MHI transfers first, explicitly queueing DL buffers, and unwinding correctly on failure.
intent_record.what: The probe function reorders initialization by removing the initial qrtr_endpoint_register() call before channel startup, replacing mhi_prepare_for_transfer_autoqueue() with mhi_prepare_for_transfer(), then registering the QRTR endpoint after transfer preparation, adding a new call to qcom_mhi_qrtr_queue_dl_buffers(), and introducing two error labels so failures unregister the endpoint and unprepare transfer state before returning.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the driver now prepares MHI transfer channels without automatic buffer queueing, explicitly registers the QRTR endpoint only after successful preparation, and manually queues downlink buffers afterward. If endpoint registration or buffer queueing fails, it cleans up by unregistering the endpoint and/or unpreparing the transfer state, preventing partially initialized probe state and ensuring the device is only exposed once data paths are ready.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix resume handling by switching from autoqueue preparation to explicit transfer setup and re-queuing downlink buffers after successful resume.
intent_record.what: In qcom_mhi_qrtr_pm_resume_early(), the call to mhi_prepare_for_transfer_autoqueue(mhi_dev) was replaced with mhi_prepare_for_transfer(mhi_dev); the error check was expanded to use braces and now immediately returns rc on failure; and the final return value was changed from returning rc to returning qcom_mhi_qrtr_queue_dl_buffers(mhi_dev).
intent_record.how: At resume time, the function now prepares the MHI device using the non-autoqueue transfer path and, if preparation succeeds, explicitly queues downlink buffers before returning. This prevents the function from silently succeeding without re-queuing buffers and ensures resume fails immediately if transfer preparation fails.

relevance_review.reason: The changes only remove redundant `.auto_queue = false` initializers while preserving the same disabled behavior via default zero-initialization. They do not address enabling/disabling DL auto_queue in QRTR-over-MHI probe ordering, nor do they change the probe-time race or NULL-dereference root cause.

The changes directly remove dependence on MHI downlink auto_queue and replace it with explicit transfer preparation and RX buffer queuing, including probe-order and resume fixes. That matches the root cause of a probe-time race where auto_queue could trigger dl_callback before qrtr_mhi_dev was fully initialized, causing NULL dereferences.

This change only removes explicit auto-queue enablement for the AIC200 channel configuration, not the QRTR-over-MHI probe-time race or the qrtr_mhi_dev initialization/registration ordering that caused the NULL dereference.

The root cause is a probe-time race caused by QRTR-over-MHI relying on DL auto_queue invoking callbacks before driver state was initialized. This group only removes an explicit auto_queue setting in the QCN9074 channel config to use the default behavior, without directly addressing the QRTR probe ordering/race or ensuring callbacks cannot run before initialization.

This change is about RX buffer lifecycle during reset/completion handling and recycling processed buffers. The root cause is a probe-time race from MHI auto_queue invoking dl_callback before qrtr_mhi_dev was initialized/registered, leading to NULL dereferences. Buffer reset/recycling logic does not directly address that initialization race.

The change only removes an unused specialized downlink auto-queue configuration macro for header cleanup. It does not alter probe ordering, driver initialization/registration, callback timing, or the auto_queue race that caused the NULL-pointer dereference.

candidates.rationale: This registers the QRTR endpoint before MHI transfers/downlink buffering are prepared, creating the probe-time ordering window described in the root cause where callbacks can run against incompletely initialized QRTR-over-MHI state.

This explicitly enables the auto-queue-based transfer path during probe. Because auto_queue may trigger dl_callback and RX buffer queuing immediately, calling this in the old initialization flow is the direct mechanism that races with full driver state setup.

The same vulnerable reliance on auto_queue also existed in resume handling. It can re-enable the problematic callback/buffer queuing behavior without the explicit downlink preparation the fix introduced.

This configures the IPCR downlink channel to use MHI DL auto_queue, the feature identified as the root cause because it can invoke receive callbacks before QRTR-over-MHI probe has safely finished initialization.

This is another pre-fix IPCR downlink auto_queue configuration. It embodies the same unsafe reliance on automatic queuing that allowed callbacks to race with QRTR-over-MHI device registration and initialization.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the direct trigger for the vulnerable behavior: enabling MHI downlink auto_queue during probe allows dl_callback/RX buffer activity to occur immediately, before qcom_mhi_qrtr_probe() has fully finished initializing and registering stable QRTR-over-MHI state, creating the probe-time race and resulting NULL dereference.

This channel configuration enables auto_queue on the IPCR downlink channel, which is the underlying mechanism relied upon by the vulnerable receive path. With auto_queue enabled, receive callbacks and buffer queuing can occur before the QRTR-over-MHI driver has safely completed initialization.

This is another IPCR downlink configuration enabling the same unsafe auto_queue behavior on affected hardware, permitting early receive callback/buffer activity that races with QRTR-over-MHI probe initialization.

This registration occurred in the old ordering before transfer/downlink setup was safely reworked. In combination with auto_queue preparation, it formed the vulnerable initialization sequence in which callbacks could run against incompletely initialized qrtr_mhi_dev state.

The same vulnerable auto_queue-based transfer preparation was also used on resume, reintroducing the unsafe behavior by allowing MHI to automatically queue downlink buffers and invoke callbacks without the explicit, controlled re-queuing added by the fix.
